speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning, as worsening morning headaches without nausea or light sensitivity, combined with your history of heart failure and retinal flashing lights, raises the possibility of a posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) or a growing intracranial issue. Given that a cardiologist previously stated no further workup was needed despite these new neurological symptoms, I must verify the current status of your brain. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. While we wait, have you noticed any changes in your blood pressure recently?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital_Signs: Blood_Pressure 140/85 mmHg; Neurological_Examination: Cranial_Nerves Normal pupillary reactions, mild papilledema in both eyes noted during fundoscopic examination; Imaging: MRI_Brain Findings Evidence of increased intracranial pressure with signs compatible with idiopathic intracranial hypertension. No masses or lesions observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumor Cerebri). The combination of headache, visual disturbances (flashing lights), papilledema, and normal neurologic exam in a patient with heart failure points to elevated intracranial pressure without a mass lesion, likely exacerbated by obesity or medication side effects. Given the confirmed MRI findings, we should proceed with an ophthalmology referral to monitor vision and consider a therapeutic trial of acetazolamide.
